walkthroughs.body_html:
Performance in Physical Education (NEA) — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Performance in Physical Education (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Performance in Physical Education (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many bones are in the adult human skeleton?

options: Elbow
Knee
Hip
Wrist
Training as hard as possible immediately.
Gradually increasing training demands so the body keeps adapting.
Doing less over time.
Deltoid.

mcqs.q: When you flex your elbow, which muscle is the agonist?
options: Triceps brachii.
A pivot joint.
Biceps brachii.
Deltoid.

mcqs.q: What type of joint is the knee?
options: A pivot joint.
A ball and socket joint.
Deltoid.
A hinge joint.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Appendicular skeleton”?
options: Tough connective tissue joining bone to bone, stabilising joints.
Bones of arms, legs, shoulder and pelvic girdles; enables movement.
Freely movable joint with synovial fluid; e.g., hinge (elbow), ball-and-socket (hip).
Skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum; protects vital organs.

options: Freely movable joint with synovial fluid; e.g., hinge (elbow), ball-and-socket (hip).
